messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For French, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | **Tant'** | Intensifier of the following adjective | Use French adverb **« si »** to convey “so”; **BT:** *so* | | **è** | Copular link between subject (implicit “it”) and predicate adjective | Render with **« est »** (3sg present of *être*); **BT:** *is* | | **amara** | Predicate adjective describing the subject | Translate as **« amère »** (feminine adjective); **BT:** *bitter* | | **che** | Introduces the comparative clause | Use **« que »** as comparative subordinator; **BT:** *that* | | **poco** | Marks a slight degree of the comparative increase | Render with **« un peu »** (degree modifier); **BT:** *little* | | **è** | Copular verb in the comparative clause | Use **« est »** again; **BT:** *is* | | **più** | Indicates that the second term exceeds the first | Translate as **« plus »** (comparative adverb); **BT:** *more* | | **morte** | Entity being compared; the “more” element | Render as **« mort »** (feminine noun); **BT:** *death* | | **ma** | Connects this clause to the preceding one | Use **« mais »** (coordinating conjunction); **BT:** *but* | | **per** | Marks purpose of the infinitive clause | Translate as **« pour »** (preposition of purpose); **BT:** *in order to* | | **trattar** | Main verb of the purpose clause (to discuss) | Use infinitive **« traiter »**; **BT:** *to treat* | | **del** | Links the verb *trattar* to its object | Render as **« du »** (de + le) before masculine noun; **BT:** *of the* | | **ben** | Object of discussion | Translate as **« bien »** (masc. noun “good”); **BT:** *good* | | **ch'** | Introduces relative clause specifying the good | Use **« que »** (relative pronoun); **BT:** *that* | | **i'** | Subject of the relative clause | Render as **« je »** (first‑person pronoun); **BT:** *I* | | **vi** | Locative reference to the place where the good was found | Translate as **« là »** (adverb of place); **BT:** *there* | | **trovai** | Action performed by the speaker in the relative clause | Use passé simple **« trouvai »** (or literary **« trouvai »**); **BT:** *found* | | **dirò** | Main verb of the sentence, future intention | Render as **« dirai »** (future 1sg of *dire*); **BT:** *I will tell* | | **de** | Introduces the noun phrase that follows | Use **« des »** (de + les) before plural; **BT:** *of the* | | **l'altre** | Modifies *cose* to indicate a distinct set | Translate as **« autres »** (adjective preceding noun); **BT:** *the other* | | **cose** | Direct object of *dirò* | Render as **« choses »** (feminine plural noun); **BT:** *things* | | **ch'** | Introduces relative clause specifying the things | Use **« que »** (relative pronoun); **BT:** *that* | | **i'** | Subject of the relative clause | Render as **« je »**; **BT:** *I* | | **v'** | Locative reference to where the things were seen | Translate as **« là »** (same as earlier); **BT:** *there* | | **ho** | Auxiliary for the perfect construction | Use **« ai »** (present of *avoir*); **BT:** *have* | | **scorte** | Main verb of the perfect relative clause | Render as past participle **« vu »** (from *voir*) in compound tense; **BT:** *seen* |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Output: bullet list only; one line per source line. Format: - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Rules: each phrase is directly placeable (no glue-only fragments) and covers the line’s main predicate + required linkage. Hook: satisfy Step 2 requirements for that line (incl. back-translation checks). Comparatives: preserve ordering (A>B ⇔ B<A is OK) and degree; at least one phrase must make both recoverable. No punctuation inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: Si amère est‑elle que la mort est un peu plus / Tant d’amertume que la mort dépasse légèrement / Aussi amère que la mort est à peine plus - Line 8: mais pour traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé là / mais afin de parler du bien que j’ai découvert ici / mais dans le but de discuter du bien que j’ai trouvé sur place - Line 9: je dirai des autres choses que j’ai vues là / je raconterai les autres choses que j’ai observées ici / je relaterai les autres choses que j’ai aperçues sur place

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Task: Assemble Step3 phrases into French lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 phrases as contiguous substrings; reorder within line as needed. Allowed edits: insert only function-words/morphology for grammatical joining; no new content words. Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary Step3 phrase: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - Si amère est‑elle que la mort est un peu plus
**Assembly Notes:** - none (phrase used as‑is)
**Target Text:** Si amère est‑elle que la mort est un peu plus;
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - mais pour traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé là
**Assembly Notes:** - none (phrase used as‑is)
**Target Text:** mais pour traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé là,
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - je dirai des autres choses que j’ai vues là
**Assembly Notes:** - none (phrase used as‑is)
**Target Text:** je dirai des autres choses que j’ai vues là.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step4 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 7 Target Text: Si amère est‑elle que la mort est un peu plus; Back-Translation: “Is it bitter that death is a little more?” Reference Translation: “So bitter is it that death is little more.” Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <FAIL> Meaning Drift <FAIL> Comparative Orientation <FAIL> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text: Si amère est‑elle que la mort est un peu plus amère;
- Line 8 Target Text: mais pour traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé là, Back-Translation: “but to treat the good that I found there” Reference Translation: “But in order to treat of the good that there I found,” Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <OK> Meaning Drift <OK> Comparative Orientation <N/A> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text: (none)
- Line 9 Target Text: je dirai des autres choses que j’ai vues là. Back-Translation: “I will say of the other things that I have seen there.” Reference Translation: “I will tell of the other things that I have seen there.” Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <OK> Meaning Drift <OK> Comparative Orientation <N/A> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text: (none)
```text Si amère est‑elle que la mort est un peu plus amère; mais pour traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé là, je dirai des autres choses que j’ai vues là. ```
